## Download and use this snapshot

This page describes the published files in `nicktempleman/csoai-gspc-axis-corpus`. Treat them as a dated snapshot: use the observation dates and limitations in the files and source notes below. A page edit does not refresh the measurements.

With the Kaggle CLI installed and authenticated:

```bash
kaggle datasets download -d nicktempleman/csoai-gspc-axis-corpus -p ./dataset --unzip
```

Start by inspecting `gspc-axis.jsonl`. Keep its original bytes and record the Kaggle version before transforming or comparing results.

Published files include:

- `README.md`
- `eval.yaml`
- `dataset.sig`
- `dataset.json`
- `manifest.jsonl`
- `gspc-axis.jsonl`

[Current GSPC board](https://councilof.ai/api/gspc) · [Methodology](https://councilof.ai/methodology/) · [Verify supported signed records](https://councilof.ai/gspc-verify/) · [Corrections](https://councilof.ai/claim-maintenance)

Apply the licence shown on this dataset. Published by Council of AI — Council for the Safety of Artificial Intelligence, operated by CSOAI Ltd. Measurement is not certification; a mirror or package is not evidence of current board admission or benchmark leadership.

**Independent measurement of GSPC axis prompts and responses. Not a certification.**

- Verify any card free: https://councilof.ai/gspc-verify/ · Catalog: https://councilof.ai/catalog.json · Methodology: https://councilof.ai/methodology/
- Live board: https://councilof.ai/api/gspc (read counts live; none are typed here)

> **Mirror.** This is a copy of https://huggingface.co/datasets/csoai/gspc-axis-corpus at revision `e7a5bcbaa5ad79a2be3e8446bfd73173c43361d2`, made 2026-10-07. The Hugging Face copy is the original; if the two differ, it wins.

# GSPC axis transcripts — prompts and full responses

The transcript corpus behind graded runs. Each row of `gspc-axis.jsonl` carries the
`axis`, the `model`, the `prompt` it was given and the full `response` it returned. This is the raw material
a grader reads — publishing it is what lets a stranger re-grade our runs instead of trusting our grades.
